thesis: Fiscal Q4 2026, reported 2026-07-29, is a confirmed company-disclosed beat: revenue $90.01B against $87.62B expected and adjusted EPS $4.74 against $4.24 expected, with Azure growth accelerating to 43%, an Azure guide raised to 45%, commercial RPO of $678B (+84%) and Copilot at 30 million seats. The 60-day move of +39% is that print being repriced, not a drift. The strongest counter-case is that the AI build-out is a margin trap — capex intensity rising faster than the revenue it funds; that does not change the read here because the company guided to steady 2026 capital expenditures while disclosing $678B of contracted, already-committed backlog, so the spend is being matched to signed demand rather than to speculative capacity. Open regulatory exposure (EU DMA cloud inquiries opened Nov 2025, a UK CMA strategic-market-status recommendation, a continuing US FTC probe) is real but none of it has a scheduled ruling, hearing or compliance deadline disclosed in the next ~90 days, so it is narrative rather than a dated risk.
invalidation: Azure growth decelerates below the raised 45% guide, or a subsequent quarter shows capex rising while RPO conversion stalls

thesis: Q2 2026, reported 2026-08-04, was a company-disclosed record: revenue $392.4M, up 104% year over year, a beat on both revenue and earnings, with Q3 guidance of $540-560M (about 40% sequential growth at the midpoint) above what analysts expected. Against that, the position is down 36.5% over 60 days and 12% since the print. The explanation reported is that the four sessions before the release, not the release itself, drove the move — a rally that ran ahead of the numbers and then unwound — with higher operating expenses from continued roadmap investment as a secondary drag. That is a positioning and sentiment explanation rather than a disclosed fundamental deterioration, and this run could not settle whether the de-rating stops there, so the evidence is unresolved rather than clean. The disclosed operating picture still supports holding: growth accelerating, guidance raised, and the FY2026 Q2 10-Q states the company is not a party to any material pending legal proceedings as of 2026-06-30, so there is no dated legal overhang.
invalidation: Q3 revenue lands below the guided $540M floor, or gross margin compresses while operating expenses keep climbing

thesis: The company raised 2026 revenue guidance to $950M-$1.05B, citing prescription trends and early uptake of newly approved Lifyorli (relacorilant) in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer — a confirmed, company-disclosed raise, and the position is up 29.6% over 60 days and sits 9.9% below its 52-week high. The read is not clean, though, because two things point the other way and neither is settled. First, the Federal Circuit affirmed on 2026-02-19 that Teva's generic Korlym does not infringe the '214 or '800 patents; Corcept filed a petition for rehearing en banc on 2026-04-22 and no decision date is disclosed, so the durability of the Korlym base that funds the launch is genuinely open. Second, the FDA refused approval of relacorilant in Cushing's syndrome despite positive Phase 3 ROSELLA data; the NDA has been resubmitted with additional analyses and the company anticipates a six-month review, so that outcome is pending rather than decided. The guidance raise postdates the appellate loss, which is a point in its favour, but with an undated en banc ruling and an unfinished FDA review both capable of moving the read, this suggests continued support for holding rather than a resolved case.
invalidation: the en banc petition is denied and generic Korlym erosion shows up in a guidance cut, or the resubmitted Cushing's NDA draws a second refusal

thesis: The disclosed picture still supports holding: fiscal 2027 guidance of $167B (plus or minus $2B), an AI-optimized server revenue target raised to roughly $60B for FY2027, and a Q2 FY2027 target of $44-45B revenue on $4.80 adjusted EPS with about $15.5B of AI server sales, after the stock set an all-time high of $484.50 on 2026-08-12. The 60-day move is +10%, and the position sits 11.5% below its 52-week high. The decisive point for conviction is timing rather than doubt: Q2 FY2027 results are due after the close on 2026-09-01, four days out, so every figure above is a target the company has set and not yet a print it has delivered. An unresolved binary that close, capable of reversing the read in either direction, caps this at medium no matter how well the AI server ramp has been tracking. The counter-case — that AI server revenue carries lower margins than the ISG mix it displaces — is named here but not answered by anything this run found. No lawsuit or regulatory matter naming the company was found with a scheduled ruling, hearing or deadline in the next ~90 days; the material Class V stockholder litigation was settled and approved in 2023.
invalidation: the 2026-09-01 print lands below the guided $44B revenue floor, or FY2027 AI server guidance is walked back from ~$60B

thesis: Fiscal Q2 2027, reported 2026-08-26, is a confirmed company-disclosed beat and raise: revenue $96.2B, up 106% from $46.7B a year earlier, EPS $2.22 against $1.05, data center sales of $89B against $86.33B expected, and current-quarter guidance of $108B plus or minus 2% against a $104.2B consensus, alongside a disclosed Amazon Web Services commitment to buy 2 million GPUs and adopt the new Vera CPU. The strongest counter-case is the post-print tape: shares rose about 8.7% on 2026-08-27 and then gave back 4.6% on 2026-08-28 on the heaviest volume of the window, and the stock has fallen after six of the previous eight reports. That does not change the read, because the reported pattern is expectations running ahead of results rather than results disappointing — the guide came in above consensus and the AWS order is a disclosed commitment, so the give-back reflects positioning into the print, not any disclosed deterioration. This suggests the disclosed demand is being underwritten by contracted orders rather than sentiment.
invalidation: the next quarter comes in below the $108B guide, or a major hyperscaler publicly defers committed GPU orders

thesis: Down 41.7% over 60 days, the sharpest move in this cycle's universe, and the causes are mixed rather than pointing one way. Q2 2026 beat Wall Street on both revenue and earnings, but third-quarter guidance came in slightly below an elevated consensus and triggered a single-day fall of more than 20%; Optical Communications, the AI-driven segment, grew 32% year over year to $2.07B but decelerated from 36% the prior quarter. Separately, shares fell again on a Jefferies report that Apple scrapped its planned all-glass 20th-anniversary iPhone over production yields — that is a broker's supply-chain check, not a company disclosure from either party, and this run could not confirm it against a primary source. A beat paired with a light guide, decelerating growth in the segment carrying the story, and an unconfirmed loss of a flagship design win do not add up to a clear net read in either direction, so this stays off the buy list rather than being treated as a discounted entry.
invalidation: Q3 lands at or above the guided range with Optical Communications reaccelerating, or Apple/Corning confirm the glass program is intact

thesis: Q2 2026, reported 2026-08-11, disclosed record revenue of $234M (up 62% year over year) and a $2.36B backlog, and the stock still fell roughly 10%. The reason given is execution rather than demand, and it is unresolved: Stage 1 tank production still supports delivering Neutron to the launchpad in Q4 2026, but the company stopped short of reaffirming a first flight before year-end. Alongside that, operating cash outflow widened to -$84.1M in Q2 from -$50.3M in Q1, and Q3 gross margin was guided to 29-31% GAAP against 36.1% in Q2. Record top-line growth offset by a wider burn, a guided-down margin and a launch date the company would not recommit to is a genuinely mixed picture, and the binary that matters — whether Neutron flies — has no disclosed date. Down 34.3% over 60 days and 57.3% below its 52-week high, this suggests waiting for the flight window to firm up rather than buying the drawdown.
invalidation: a firm Neutron first-flight date is disclosed and held, with Q3 gross margin landing at or above the guided range

thesis: Q2 2026 missed on both revenue and adjusted earnings, with EPS of -$0.35 against -$0.29 expected, while full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $150-200M was maintained and pro forma liquidity was reported at more than $3.7B as of 2026-06-30. The 60-day move of -33% is not primarily that print: shares fell 15.5% intraday on 2026-08-28 after Fed Chair Kevin Warsh signalled inflation is the Fed's focus, raising the odds of a rate hike — a macro repricing of a constellation being built largely on borrowed money, not a disclosed change in the business. The company also raised $1.15B of 1.625% convertible senior notes in July 2026, which management called cost-efficient and which investors read as future dilution, and it depends on third-party launch capacity after SpaceX announced schedule changes. A miss, a rate-driven selloff, fresh convertible paper and third-party launch dependence leave no clear company-specific case to underwrite an entry here.
invalidation: revenue tracks into the maintained $150-200M range on schedule and launch cadence is secured without further convertible issuance

thesis: Two things are pulling the stock down 32% over 60 days and this run cannot rank one clearly above the other. The company-specific one is disclosed and finished: a $20B common stock offering, upsized from an original $15B plan, priced roughly 210.5 million new shares at $95, and the stock now trades below that offer price at $89.33 — the dilution is arithmetic, not opinion, and it lands on a Foundry segment that posted a $2.8B operating loss in Q2 2026. The second is a broad semiconductor selloff that hit the whole sector in the same sessions, which is macro rather than company-specific. The bull counter-case — that the raise removes financing risk from the foundry roadmap — is real but unanswerable from what this run found, since the capital only converts to value if the process roadmap lands, and reported CPU share is at a three-decade low against AMD EPYC gains. Fresh dilution into deepening segment losses, with sector pressure layered on top, is not a setup to buy.
invalidation: Foundry operating losses narrow materially on a subsequent print, or the shares reclaim and hold the $95 offer price on external-customer wins

thesis: Q2 2026, released after the close on 2026-08-06, was a beat: EPS of $0.06 against a $0.01 consensus on revenue of $191.9M against $190.48M expected. What moved the stock afterwards was a separate disclosure — another $600M at-the-market equity offering — which sent shares down about 10% after hours and about 12.3% in the following pre-market. The counter-case is that the beat and the ramp behind it justify funding growth, and analyst targets moved in both directions on it (Raymond James cut to $151 from $160 at Outperform, Northland raised to $120 from $57.50 at Market Perform). That does not settle the read: a $600M ATM on a company that just printed $191.9M of quarterly revenue is a large and open-ended claim on future share count, and an ATM by construction sells into strength for as long as it is live. With the stock down 29.2% over 60 days and 54.6% below its 52-week high, the dilution overhang is the dominant near-term fact and argues against an entry.
invalidation: the ATM is exhausted or withdrawn without material issuance, or a subsequent quarter shows revenue scaling faster than share count

thesis: Fiscal Q4 2026, reported 2026-08-12, is a confirmed company-disclosed improvement: sales of $2,045.5M in the quarter and $7.12B for the full year, a swing to profitability, adjusted non-GAAP EPS of $1.74 against a $1.61 consensus and up 74% from $1.00 a year earlier, with Q1 EPS guided to $1.85-2.05 against a $1.77 consensus, plus the start of 300mm high-thermal-conductivity silicon carbide sampling to AI semiconductor customers. Against that the stock is down 28.6% over 60 days. The reported explanation is that traders unwound a crowded AI-optics trade into and after the print — described as valuation pressure rather than a new company-specific shock, with a 14.2% fall ahead of earnings and a further decline after. That is a positioning explanation, which discounts how much the drawdown says about the business but also leaves the de-rating unfinished and unresolved: nothing this run found establishes where the multiple settles. Disclosed results and guidance point up while the tape points down, and only the first of those is confirmed.
invalidation: Q1 EPS lands below the guided $1.85 floor, or optical order growth is disclosed as slowing rather than the multiple compressing

thesis: The disclosed fundamentals and the 27.6% 60-day drawdown point opposite ways. Reported fiscal 2026 revenue rose 175% year over year to $20.25B with gross margin at 84.6% in the latest quarter. The selling is attributed to a policy report rather than to the company: US officials are weighing whether to let Apple diversify memory sourcing toward China's CXMT for DRAM and YMTC for NAND, which would threaten the NAND scarcity that drove the price increases behind those numbers. That is a sector-wide and geopolitical catalyst — the same reports moved Micron and Western Digital on the same days — not a company-specific disclosure, and its outcome is a policy decision no filing this run read has settled. Estimated NAND price gains of about 70% are also expected by TrendForce to moderate to 10-15% this quarter, so some deceleration is anticipated by forecasters rather than disclosed by the company. Disclosed results still support the position, but the risk driving the price is unresolved and outside the company's control.
invalidation: US policy formally clears Chinese memory suppliers for Apple, or NAND contract pricing turns negative in a subsequent quarter

thesis: Q2 fiscal 2027, reported 2026-08-27, was a confirmed company-disclosed double beat: record revenue of $2.739B, up 37% year over year, with record EPS above guidance, a $500M increase to the FY27 revenue outlook and a $1.5B increase to FY28, and management pointing to $3B of quarterly revenue in Q3 — a full quarter earlier than the prior outlook. The stock nonetheless fell about 8% on 2026-08-28 on 2.37x its 30-bar average volume, the only volume-spike trigger in this cycle. The reported explanation is valuation after a 187% year-to-date run plus a mixed reading of the expanded Google custom-silicon agreement disclosed 2026-08-19, which attaches Marvell across the TPU stack but does so by issuing Google a warrant over 58.97 million Marvell shares at $206.58, vesting toward $120B of cumulative revenue. That warrant is the counter-case and it is not settled: it is a large disclosed equity claim whose cost is certain while the revenue that vests it is not, and one analyst read the deal as Google adding a supplier rather than displacing Broadcom. Results support the position; the equity overhang is real and unresolved.
invalidation: Q3 revenue lands below the $3B management pointed to, or Google TPU volumes attach to competitors while the warrant continues vesting

thesis: Q2 2026, reported 2026-08-12, disclosed revenue of $582.3M against $105.1M a year earlier (up 454%) and adjusted EBITDA swinging to a $236.2M profit from a $21.0M loss, with the year-end contracted power target raised to 5 gigawatts and FY2026 revenue guidance of $3.0-3.4B reaffirmed. Shares rose more than 20% above $280 on that, then round-tripped roughly 25% toward $200 after the company announced a proposed $4.5B convertible note offering on 2026-08-19, which fell about 10% on the day on dilution concerns. That financing is the counter-case and this run cannot resolve it: capital expenditure plans reported at $20-25B through 2026 against negative cash flow mean the convertible is unlikely to be the last raise, and the disclosed growth does not by itself establish that returns arrive before the funding cost compounds. The operating disclosure supports the position; the capital structure is the open question, and it is what the tape is trading.
invalidation: FY2026 revenue tracks below the reaffirmed $3.0B floor, or a further equity-linked raise arrives before contracted capacity converts to revenue

thesis: This run found no company-disclosed figure for Micron to anchor a thesis on — no earnings print was read this cycle, so the current quarter's results are unconfirmed here and are not characterised as a beat, miss or raise. What is documented is external and adverse. Shares fell 5.5% in the first minutes of 2026-08-24 on reports the administration decided to permit Apple to buy memory chips from Chinese suppliers, with CXMT and YMTC named as candidates — a policy and sector-wide catalyst that hit the memory complex together rather than Micron specifically. Separately, Netlist filed a complaint with the US International Trade Commission on 2026-08-12 alleging infringement of four patents tied to DDR5 RDIMM and MRDIMM products; that is an active proceeding but no scheduled ruling, hearing or compliance deadline in the next ~90 days was found, so it is an overhang rather than a dated event. Down 18.6% over 60 days on a sector-wide catalyst with no confirmed company disclosure to weigh against it, there is nothing company-specific here to underwrite an entry.
invalidation: a company-disclosed print confirms pricing and volumes holding, or the Chinese-supplier policy report is contradicted by an official decision

thesis: Q2 2026, reported 2026-08-12, published two figures that point opposite ways and both belong in the read. On the company's preferred basis, core revenue was $210M and core gross margin was 41%, an improvement of roughly 940 basis points from Q2 2025, adjusted loss per share was $0.05 against $0.17 expected, and full-year guidance was raised. On a GAAP basis the same quarter reported revenue of $180.1M — up 74% year over year but short of the roughly $194M expected — a net loss of $450.5M against a $309.5M profit a year earlier, GAAP gross margin of 14%, and GAAP EPS of -$2.98, missing by $1.31, with $386.6M of stock-based compensation identified as the primary driver of the reversal. The 14% after-hours fall is consistent with the GAAP set, not the core set, which is why quoting only the core figures would misread the reaction. A raised outlook and expanding core margins against a GAAP revenue miss and a $450.5M loss is unresolved evidence, and with the stock 17.2% lower over 60 days and only 11.2% above its 52-week low, that is not a case to enter on.
invalidation: GAAP revenue reaches consensus in a subsequent quarter with the loss narrowing ex-stock-compensation, or the raised full-year guidance is cut

thesis: Q2 2026, reported 2026-08-04, disclosed revenue of $7.8B, up 92% year over year against a $6.81B estimate, adjusted EBITDA up 191% to $3.5B on a $541M net loss, Connectivity revenue of $4.3B with 1.7 million net subscriber adds, and AI segment revenue up 247% to $2.6B. The 60-day move of -13.8% is largely mechanical rather than fundamental: the first post-IPO lockup expired on 2026-08-06, releasing 911.5 million insider shares and lifting the freely tradable float from 4.9% to 11.8% of shares outstanding, and analysts read much of the preceding slump — including a near-14% fall to an all-time low close of $108.27 — as anticipation of exactly that supply. The unlock day itself passed without the feared break, with shares closing up 6.1%, and the stock has since recovered to $140.98. Because the drawdown is explained as anticipatory supply pressure rather than disclosed deterioration, the disclosed beat is not what has been driving the price, and the next structural unlock — Musk cleared to sell 6.4 billion shares in mid-2027 — sits beyond this position's review horizon but keeps the supply question open.
invalidation: subscriber adds or Connectivity revenue decelerate on a subsequent print, or a further unlock tranche breaks the post-August price range

thesis: Q2 fiscal 2026 was a company-disclosed beat: revenue of $11.54B, up 50.1% year over year, non-GAAP EPS of $1.66 against a $1.6107 consensus, and data centre revenue more than doubling at +107%. The stock fell on the print anyway, on reported concerns about rising capital expenditure and margin pressure, and has continued lower with the broader semiconductor complex, leaving it down 13.7% over 60 days and about 20% below its 52-week high. The unresolved counter-case is structural rather than sentimental: the company granted OpenAI an option over up to 160 million shares, roughly a 10% stake worth about $73.1B at recent prices, so a substantial part of the AI demand being underwritten here is paid for in equity whose cost is fixed while the revenue behind it is not. The MI400 Instinct series and Helios rack ramp into Q4 2026 and Q1 2027 are guided rather than delivered, so the constructive case still depends on execution nobody has yet seen.
invalidation: MI400 or Helios timing slips from the guided Q4 2026/Q1 2027 ramp, or data centre gross margin compresses on a subsequent print
